request.spec:
A claim that is moved to another person now receives the next number in the sequence it would be
numbered in (the sheet's, or its period's when per-period numbering is on), and its old number is
never used again; a draft, having no number, gets none. CLAIM_REASSIGNED carries the new number.
Moving claims together follows the same rule, in list order.

agent.result_text:
A moved claim now gets a new number, and all 4 tests in the spec pass with `bin/e2e`.

The change is all in `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/claim/ClaimReassign.java`, the move logic that the single and the bulk reassign share:

- **Numbered claims:** after every check has passed, an OPEN or PENDING claim being moved takes the next number. It uses the same rule as opening a claim: the sheet's sequence, or its period's sequence (by the claim's due-by date) when per-period numbering is on. The old number stays used and is never handed out again.
- **Drafts:** a draft has no number and still gets none when it is moved.
- **Audit:** `CLAIM_REASSIGNED` shows the new number, or no number for a draft.
- **Bulk moves:** these already handled claims one at a time in list order, so they number in that order without further changes.

A refused move still writes nothing, because the number is only taken once every check has passed. The front end needed no change, since it shows the number the server sends back. I also updated the class's doc comment, which used to say a moved claim keeps its number.

One thing to be aware of: any record that pointed at a claim by its old number will no longer match it after a move. That includes a correction that names the number of the claim it corrects. This follows from the request and the tests don't cover it.
